PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient ID: [redacted ID]
Maternal Age: 40 years
Gestational Age: 13 weeks
Specimen Type: Chorionic villi (uncultured)
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Abnormal ultrasound findings in pregnancy

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Rapid aneuploidy detection for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from uncultured chorionic villi. QF-PCR analysis was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers specific to chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y. Fragment analysis was carried out by capillary electrophoresis. Peak area ratios were calculated for informative markers.

RESULTS

CHROMOSOME 18: ABNORMAL - TRISOMY 18 DETECTED

Informative markers showing triallelic patterns:
• D18S976 (18p11.31): Three alleles detected, ratio 1:1:1
• D18S819 (18q11.2): Three alleles detected, ratio 1:1:1
• D18S847 (18q12.1): Three alleles detected, ratio 1:1:1
• D18S535 (18q12.3): Three alleles detected, ratio 1:1:1
• D18S978 (18q12.3): Three alleles detected, ratio 1:1:1

CHROMOSOME 13: Normal diallelic pattern
Informative markers: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628

CHROMOSOME 21: Normal diallelic pattern
Informative markers: D21S1435, D21S11, D21S1270, D21S1411

SEX CHROMOSOMES: Female (XX)
AMELOGENIN: X,X
X chromosome markers: Normal diallelic pattern
Y chromosome markers: Not detected

INTERPRETATION
This QF-PCR result indicates TRISOMY 18 (Edwards syndrome) in the fetal sample. Five informative markers on chromosome 18 all demonstrate triallelic patterns consistent with three copies of chromosome 18. The findings for chromosomes 13 and 21 are normal, with no evidence of trisomy. The sex chromosome complement is female (XX).

These molecular findings are concordant with the reported ultrasound abnormalities and are consistent with a diagnosis of Edwards syndrome.

LIMITATIONS
• This test assumes the absence of significant maternal cell contamination
• Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected by this method
• This test does not exclude other chromosomal abnormalities or structural rearrangements
• QF-PCR does not provide information about the mechanism of trisomy (meiotic vs mitotic origin)

RECOMMENDATIONS
Follow-up karyotype analysis of G-banded chromosomes from cultured chorionic villi is recommended to:
1. Confirm the trisomy 18 finding
2. Exclude mosaicism
3. Rule out structural chromosomal abnormalities
4. Provide a complete cytogenetic assessment

Genetic counseling is strongly recommended to discuss these results, prognosis, and reproductive options.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
